findings.title: Runner regressions pass CI unchecked
findings.description: Removing the `python3 -m unittest discover -s yantra -p 'test_*.py'` step eliminates the only CI invocation of the runner’s unit tests. When a pull request changes `yantra/runner.py`, neither the remaining Rust checks nor the new guard workflow runs those tests, so a failing runner test no longer prevents the change from merging.

findings.title: A pull request can silence the guard
findings.description: The Guard step redirects the base-branch script into `ci/guard.sh`, but shell redirection follows a symlink supplied by the pull request. If the pull request replaces that file with a symlink to `/dev/null`, the fetched script is discarded and `sh ci/guard.sh` exits successfully without running the checks that reject combined engine and measurement changes.

findings.title: A pull request can skip the guard in CI
findings.description: The new `Guard` step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` fetches the base branch's `ci/guard.sh` only when the workflow runs, but the workflow file itself is read from the pull request's head. A pull request that deletes this step and also changes engine code reaches CI with no guard and still passes, which is the failure case of rule 5040763; the PR description discloses this gap, but the failure criteria still hold until the workflow file is protected.
